turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, a little stressed, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm seventeen, going for a Christmas job at a toy shop. What will they ask?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Probably simple things. When you're free, why you want to work there, and how you'd handle a busy shop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Changing the subject, My daughter starts secondary school in September and we're working out how she'll get there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ooh, can you just listen while I run through the choices? Then I'll ask what you think.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The school bus picks up at the end of our road, but it leaves really early, at ten past seven.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She could take the public bus with her friends, it's later but involves one change in town.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or I drop her at the train station on my way to work, and she takes one stop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, that's everything. Now you can weigh in.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The school bus is the simplest and safest, even if the early start hurts. The public bus with friends builds independence, but the change adds a chance to miss a connection. The train is quick, though it ties her to your work schedule.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What do I say for why I want to work there? Money?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Money's honest, but add something else. Maybe that you like helping people or that you know lots about games and toys.
